name: LLM Guard
tagline: Security toolkit that sanitizes and screens LLM prompts and responses.
description: LLM Guard is a security toolkit for large language model applications. It runs prompts and model responses through configurable scanners — prompt-injection and jailbreak detection, PII redaction, toxicity and bias checks, and secrets scanning — to sanitize input and validate output before it reaches users. It ships as a Python library you wrap around your own LLM calls, with the scanners running locally.
insight: Maintained by Protect AI, which Palo Alto Networks acquired in 2025 and folded into its Prisma AIRS platform.

modelSupport.notes: Wraps any LLM; scanners run locally, so prompts aren't sent to a third-party service.

edge: Runs entirely self-hosted and free, with composable input and output scanners — no per-call cost or sending prompts to a hosted guardrail API.
pros: Self-hosted — data stays in your stack
cons: Python library — you build the integration
Tuning needed to cut false positives
